# Supported functions

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs:functions` from src/engine/functions. Do not edit by hand. -->

Gridline implements **112 functions** with its own evaluator (no third-party formula engine). Arguments in `[brackets]` are optional; `...` means the previous argument can repeat.

| Category | Count | Functions |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| [Math](#math) | 31 | SUM, PRODUCT, ABS, ROUND, ROUNDUP, ROUNDDOWN, INT, TRUNC, MOD, POWER, SQRT, EXP, LN, LOG, LOG10, PI, SIGN, CEILING, FLOOR, FACT, RAND, RANDBETWEEN, SUMPRODUCT, SUMSQ, SUMIF, SUMIFS, SIN, COS, TAN, RADIANS, DEGREES |
| [Statistical](#statistical) | 17 | AVERAGE, AVERAGEIF, MIN, MAX, MEDIAN, MODE, STDEV, STDEVP, VAR, VARP, COUNT, COUNTA, COUNTBLANK, COUNTIF, COUNTIFS, LARGE, SMALL |
| [Logical](#logical) | 11 | IF, IFS, AND, OR, XOR, NOT, TRUE, FALSE, IFERROR, IFNA, SWITCH |
| [Text](#text) | 21 | CONCAT, CONCATENATE, TEXTJOIN, LEN, UPPER, LOWER, PROPER, TRIM, LEFT, RIGHT, MID, FIND, SEARCH, SUBSTITUTE, REPLACE, REPT, TEXT, VALUE, EXACT, CHAR, CODE |
| [Lookup](#lookup) | 10 | VLOOKUP, HLOOKUP, XLOOKUP, INDEX, MATCH, CHOOSE, ROW, COLUMN, ROWS, COLUMNS |
| [Information](#information) | 11 | ISBLANK, ISNUMBER, ISTEXT, ISLOGICAL, ISERROR, ISERR, ISNA, ISEVEN, ISODD, TYPE, NA |
| [Date](#date) | 11 | DATE, TODAY, NOW, YEAR, MONTH, DAY, HOUR, MINUTE, WEEKDAY, DAYS, EDATE |

## Math

| Function | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SUM(number1, [number2], ...)` | Adds all numbers in the arguments. Text and logical values inside ranges are ignored. | `=SUM(A1:A10, 5)` |
| `PRODUCT(number1, [number2], ...)` | Multiplies all numbers in the arguments. | `=PRODUCT(A1:A3)` |
| `ABS(number)` | Absolute value of a number. | `=ABS(-4)` |
| `ROUND(number, [num_digits])` | Rounds a number to a number of digits (half away from zero). Negative digits round to the left of the decimal point. | `=ROUND(3.14159, 2)` |
| `ROUNDUP(number, [num_digits])` | Rounds a number away from zero. | `=ROUNDUP(3.141, 1)` |
| `ROUNDDOWN(number, [num_digits])` | Rounds a number toward zero. | `=ROUNDDOWN(3.149, 2)` |
| `INT(number)` | Rounds a number down to the nearest integer. | `=INT(-3.5)` |
| `TRUNC(number, [num_digits])` | Truncates a number by removing its fractional part (or digits beyond num_digits). | `=TRUNC(8.97, 1)` |
| `MOD(number, divisor)` | Remainder after division. The result has the same sign as the divisor. | `=MOD(10, 3)` |
| `POWER(number, power)` | Raises a number to a power. | `=POWER(2, 10)` |
| `SQRT(number)` | Positive square root of a number. | `=SQRT(16)` |
| `EXP(number)` | e raised to the power of a number. | `=EXP(1)` |
| `LN(number)` | Natural logarithm of a positive number. | `=LN(10)` |
| `LOG(number, [base])` | Logarithm of a number to a base (default 10). | `=LOG(8, 2)` |
| `LOG10(number)` | Base-10 logarithm of a number. | `=LOG10(1000)` |
| `PI()` | The number π (3.14159265358979). | `=PI()*2^2` |
| `SIGN(number)` | Returns 1 for positive numbers, -1 for negative numbers and 0 for zero. | `=SIGN(-12)` |
| `CEILING(number, [significance])` | Rounds a number up to the nearest multiple of significance (default 1). | `=CEILING(4.3, 0.5)` |
| `FLOOR(number, [significance])` | Rounds a number down to the nearest multiple of significance (default 1). | `=FLOOR(4.7, 0.5)` |
| `FACT(number)` | Factorial of a non-negative integer. | `=FACT(5)` |
| `RAND()` | A random number between 0 (inclusive) and 1 (exclusive). Recalculated on every change. *(volatile)* | `=RAND()` |
| `RANDBETWEEN(bottom, top)` | A random integer between bottom and top (inclusive). Recalculated on every change. *(volatile)* | `=RANDBETWEEN(1, 6)` |
| `SUMPRODUCT(array1, [array2], ...)` | Multiplies corresponding entries of equally sized ranges and returns the sum of the products. | `=SUMPRODUCT(B2:B5, C2:C5)` |
| `SUMSQ(number1, [number2], ...)` | Sum of the squares of the arguments. | `=SUMSQ(3, 4)` |
| `SUMIF(range, criterion, [sum_range])` | Sums the cells that meet a criterion, e.g. ">10", "apple", "<>0" or "a*". | `=SUMIF(A2:A10, ">5", B2:B10)` |
| `SUMIFS(sum_range, criteria_range1, criterion1, [criteria_range2, criterion2], ...)` | Sums the cells in sum_range where every criteria range meets its criterion. | `=SUMIFS(C2:C10, A2:A10, "East", B2:B10, ">100")` |
| `SIN(angle)` | Sine of an angle given in radians. | `=SIN(PI()/2)` |
| `COS(angle)` | Cosine of an angle given in radians. | `=COS(0)` |
| `TAN(angle)` | Tangent of an angle given in radians. | `=TAN(PI()/4)` |
| `RADIANS(degrees)` | Converts degrees to radians. | `=RADIANS(180)` |
| `DEGREES(radians)` | Converts radians to degrees. | `=DEGREES(PI())` |

## Statistical

| Function | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AVERAGE(number1, [number2], ...)` | Arithmetic mean of the numbers in the arguments. | `=AVERAGE(B2:B20)` |
| `AVERAGEIF(range, criterion, [average_range])` | Average of the cells that meet a criterion. | `=AVERAGEIF(A2:A10, "East", B2:B10)` |
| `MIN(number1, [number2], ...)` | Smallest number in the arguments (0 if there are none). | `=MIN(A1:A100)` |
| `MAX(number1, [number2], ...)` | Largest number in the arguments (0 if there are none). | `=MAX(A1:A100)` |
| `MEDIAN(number1, [number2], ...)` | Median (middle value) of the numbers. | `=MEDIAN(A1:A9)` |
| `MODE(number1, [number2], ...)` | Most frequently occurring number. | `=MODE(1, 2, 2, 3)` |
| `STDEV(number1, [number2], ...)` | Sample standard deviation. | `=STDEV(A1:A10)` |
| `STDEVP(number1, [number2], ...)` | Population standard deviation. | `=STDEVP(A1:A10)` |
| `VAR(number1, [number2], ...)` | Sample variance. | `=VAR(A1:A10)` |
| `VARP(number1, [number2], ...)` | Population variance. | `=VARP(A1:A10)` |
| `COUNT(value1, [value2], ...)` | Counts how many values are numbers. | `=COUNT(A1:A100)` |
| `COUNTA(value1, [value2], ...)` | Counts values that are not empty (numbers, text, logical values and errors). | `=COUNTA(A:A)` |
| `COUNTBLANK(range)` | Counts empty cells (and cells containing empty text) in a range. | `=COUNTBLANK(A1:C10)` |
| `COUNTIF(range, criterion)` | Counts the cells in a range that meet a criterion, e.g. ">10", "apple" or "a*". | `=COUNTIF(B2:B100, ">50")` |
| `COUNTIFS(criteria_range1, criterion1, [criteria_range2, criterion2], ...)` | Counts positions where every criteria range meets its criterion. | `=COUNTIFS(A2:A10, "East", B2:B10, ">100")` |
| `LARGE(array, k)` | The k-th largest number in a range. | `=LARGE(A1:A10, 2)` |
| `SMALL(array, k)` | The k-th smallest number in a range. | `=SMALL(A1:A10, 2)` |

## Logical

| Function | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `IF(logical_test, value_if_true, [value_if_false])` | Returns one value if a condition is TRUE and another if it is FALSE. Only the chosen branch is evaluated. | `=IF(A1>=50, "Pass", "Fail")` |
| `IFS(condition1, value1, [condition2, value2], ...)` | Returns the value for the first condition that is TRUE. | `=IFS(A1>=90, "A", A1>=80, "B", TRUE, "C")` |
| `AND(logical1, [logical2], ...)` | TRUE if all arguments are TRUE. | `=AND(A1>0, B1>0)` |
| `OR(logical1, [logical2], ...)` | TRUE if any argument is TRUE. | `=OR(A1="yes", B1="yes")` |
| `XOR(logical1, [logical2], ...)` | TRUE if an odd number of arguments are TRUE. | `=XOR(TRUE, FALSE)` |
| `NOT(logical)` | Reverses a logical value. | `=NOT(A1>10)` |
| `TRUE()` | The logical value TRUE. | `=TRUE()` |
| `FALSE()` | The logical value FALSE. | `=FALSE()` |
| `IFERROR(value, value_if_error)` | Returns value_if_error if the first argument is an error, otherwise the first argument. | `=IFERROR(A1/B1, 0)` |
| `IFNA(value, value_if_na)` | Returns value_if_na if the first argument is #N/A, otherwise the first argument. | `=IFNA(VLOOKUP(D1, A:B, 2, FALSE), "Not found")` |
| `SWITCH(expression, case1, value1, [case2, value2], ..., [default])` | Compares an expression against a list of cases and returns the value of the first match. | `=SWITCH(A1, 1, "One", 2, "Two", "Many")` |

## Text

| Function | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CONCAT(text1, [text2], ...)` | Joins text values; ranges are joined in row-major order. | `=CONCAT(A1, " ", B1)` |
| `CONCATENATE(text1, [text2], ...)` | Joins several text values into one. | `=CONCATENATE("Q", 1, "-", 2024)` |
| `TEXTJOIN(delimiter, ignore_empty, text1, [text2], ...)` | Joins text values with a delimiter, optionally skipping empty values. | `=TEXTJOIN(", ", TRUE, A1:A5)` |
| `LEN(text)` | Number of characters in a text value. | `=LEN(A1)` |
| `UPPER(text)` | Converts text to upper case. | `=UPPER("hello")` |
| `LOWER(text)` | Converts text to lower case. | `=LOWER("HELLO")` |
| `PROPER(text)` | Capitalizes the first letter of each word. | `=PROPER("ada lovelace")` |
| `TRIM(text)` | Removes leading/trailing spaces and collapses repeated spaces between words. | `=TRIM("  too   many  spaces ")` |
| `LEFT(text, [num_chars])` | The first characters of a text value (default 1). | `=LEFT("Spreadsheet", 6)` |
| `RIGHT(text, [num_chars])` | The last characters of a text value (default 1). | `=RIGHT("Spreadsheet", 5)` |
| `MID(text, start_num, num_chars)` | Characters from the middle of a text value, starting at start_num (1-based). | `=MID("Spreadsheet", 7, 5)` |
| `FIND(find_text, within_text, [start_num])` | Position (1-based) of find_text in within_text. Case-sensitive. | `=FIND("s", "Sheets")` |
| `SEARCH(find_text, within_text, [start_num])` | Position (1-based) of find_text in within_text. Case-insensitive, supports * and ? wildcards. | `=SEARCH("sheet", "Spreadsheet")` |
| `SUBSTITUTE(text, old_text, new_text, [instance_num])` | Replaces occurrences of old_text with new_text (all of them, or only the given instance). | `=SUBSTITUTE("a-b-c", "-", "+")` |
| `REPLACE(old_text, start_num, num_chars, new_text)` | Replaces num_chars characters starting at start_num with new_text. | `=REPLACE("2023-report", 1, 4, "2024")` |
| `REPT(text, number_times)` | Repeats text a number of times. | `=REPT("★", 3)` |
| `TEXT(value, format_text)` | Formats a number as text using a pattern such as "0.00", "#,##0", "0%", "$#,##0.00" or "yyyy-mm-dd". | `=TEXT(1234.5, "$#,##0.00")` |
| `VALUE(text)` | Converts text that looks like a number into a number. | `=VALUE("42.5")` |
| `EXACT(text1, text2)` | TRUE if two text values are exactly the same (case-sensitive). | `=EXACT("Word", "word")` |
| `CHAR(number)` | The character with the given character code. | `=CHAR(65)` |
| `CODE(text)` | Character code of the first character of a text value. | `=CODE("A")` |

## Lookup

| Function | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `VLOOKUP(lookup_value, table_array, col_index, [range_lookup])` | Looks for a value in the first column of a table and returns the value in the same row from another column. range_lookup FALSE = exact match; TRUE (default) = approximate match on sorted data. | `=VLOOKUP("Pears", A2:C10, 3, FALSE)` |
| `HLOOKUP(lookup_value, table_array, row_index, [range_lookup])` | Looks for a value in the first row of a table and returns the value in the same column from another row. | `=HLOOKUP("Q2", A1:E3, 2, FALSE)` |
| `XLOOKUP(lookup_value, lookup_array, return_array, [if_not_found], [match_mode], [search_mode])` | Searches lookup_array and returns the matching item from return_array. match_mode: 0 exact (default), -1 exact or next smaller, 1 exact or next larger, 2 wildcard. search_mode: 1 first-to-last, -1 last-to-first. | `=XLOOKUP(E2, A2:A100, C2:C100, "Missing")` |
| `INDEX(array, row_num, [col_num])` | The value at a given row and column of a range (1-based). A row or column of 0 returns the whole column or row. | `=INDEX(A2:C10, 4, 2)` |
| `MATCH(lookup_value, lookup_array, [match_type])` | Relative position of a value in a row or column. match_type 0 = exact, 1 (default) = largest value ≤ lookup (ascending data), -1 = smallest value ≥ lookup (descending data). | `=MATCH("Kiwi", A2:A20, 0)` |
| `CHOOSE(index_num, value1, [value2], ...)` | Returns the value at position index_num from the list of values. Only the chosen value is evaluated. | `=CHOOSE(2, "Low", "Medium", "High")` |
| `ROW([reference])` | Row number of a reference, or of the current cell when omitted. | `=ROW(B7)` |
| `COLUMN([reference])` | Column number of a reference, or of the current cell when omitted. | `=COLUMN(D1)` |
| `ROWS(range)` | Number of rows in a range. | `=ROWS(A1:C10)` |
| `COLUMNS(range)` | Number of columns in a range. | `=COLUMNS(A1:C10)` |

## Information

| Function | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ISBLANK(value)` | TRUE if the referenced cell is empty. | `=ISBLANK(A1)` |
| `ISNUMBER(value)` | TRUE if the value is a number. | `=ISNUMBER(A1)` |
| `ISTEXT(value)` | TRUE if the value is text. | `=ISTEXT(A1)` |
| `ISLOGICAL(value)` | TRUE if the value is TRUE or FALSE. | `=ISLOGICAL(A1)` |
| `ISERROR(value)` | TRUE if the value is any error (#N/A, #DIV/0!, #VALUE!, ...). | `=ISERROR(A1/B1)` |
| `ISERR(value)` | TRUE if the value is an error other than #N/A. | `=ISERR(A1)` |
| `ISNA(value)` | TRUE if the value is the #N/A error. | `=ISNA(MATCH("x", A:A, 0))` |
| `ISEVEN(number)` | TRUE if the integer part of the number is even. | `=ISEVEN(4)` |
| `ISODD(number)` | TRUE if the integer part of the number is odd. | `=ISODD(3)` |
| `TYPE(value)` | Type code of a value: 1 number (or empty), 2 text, 4 logical, 16 error, 64 range. | `=TYPE("abc")` |
| `NA()` | Returns the #N/A error, used to mark missing data. | `=NA()` |

## Date

| Function | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DATE(year, month, day)` | Serial number of a date. Months and days outside their range roll over (e.g. month 13 = January next year). Format the cell as Date to display it. | `=DATE(2024, 12, 31)` |
| `TODAY()` | Serial number of today's date. Recalculated on every change. *(volatile)* | `=TODAY()` |
| `NOW()` | Serial number of the current date and time. Recalculated on every change. *(volatile)* | `=NOW()` |
| `YEAR(date)` | Year of a date. | `=YEAR(TODAY())` |
| `MONTH(date)` | Month (1-12) of a date. | `=MONTH("2024-03-15")` |
| `DAY(date)` | Day of the month (1-31) of a date. | `=DAY(DATE(2024, 3, 15))` |
| `HOUR(time)` | Hour (0-23) of a date/time serial number. | `=HOUR(NOW())` |
| `MINUTE(time)` | Minute (0-59) of a date/time serial number. | `=MINUTE(NOW())` |
| `WEEKDAY(date, [return_type])` | Day of the week. return_type 1 (default): Sunday=1..Saturday=7; 2: Monday=1..Sunday=7; 3: Monday=0..Sunday=6. | `=WEEKDAY("2024-03-15", 2)` |
| `DAYS(end_date, start_date)` | Number of days between two dates. | `=DAYS("2024-12-25", TODAY())` |
| `EDATE(start_date, months)` | The date a number of months before or after a start date. | `=EDATE(DATE(2024, 1, 31), 1)` |

## Operators

From lowest to highest precedence (same as Excel):

| Operator | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `=` `<>` `<` `>` `<=` `>=` | Comparison (text is compared case-insensitively) | `=A1>=10` |
| `&` | Text concatenation | `=A1 & " " & B1` |
| `+` `-` | Addition, subtraction | `=A1-B1` |
| `*` `/` | Multiplication, division | `=A1/B1` |
| `^` | Exponentiation (left-associative: `2^3^2` = 64) | `=2^10` |
| `%` | Postfix percent | `=50%` |
| `-` `+` (prefix) | Negation; binds tighter than `^`, so `-2^2` = 4 | `=-A1` |
| `:` | Range: `A1:B5`, whole columns `A:C`, whole rows `2:5` | `=SUM(A:A)` |

## Criteria syntax (COUNTIF, SUMIF, AVERAGEIF, COUNTIFS, SUMIFS)

| Criterion | Matches |
| --- | --- |
| `5` or `"5"` | Cells equal to 5 |
| `">10"`, `"<=3"`, `"<>0"` | Numeric comparison |
| `"apple"` | Text equal to apple (case-insensitive) |
| `"a*"`, `"?at"` | Wildcards: `*` any characters, `?` one character, `~*` a literal `*` |
| `"<>apple"` | Anything except apple |
| `""` / `"="` | Empty cells |
| `"<>"` | Non-empty cells |

## Error values

| Error | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `#DIV/0!` | A number was divided by zero or by an empty cell. |
| `#VALUE!` | A value has the wrong type for the operation, e.g. text used in arithmetic. |
| `#REF!` | A reference points outside the sheet or to a cell that no longer exists. |
| `#NAME?` | The formula uses a function or name that does not exist. |
| `#N/A` | A lookup did not find the value it was searching for. |
| `#NUM!` | A calculation produced an invalid number (e.g. square root of a negative number). |
| `#NULL!` | Two ranges that do not intersect were combined. |
| `#CIRC!` | The formula depends on its own result, directly or through other cells. |
| `#ERROR!` | The formula could not be parsed: it contains a syntax error. |
